answers.name: Labrador retriever
answers.fact: Despite the name, the breed began in Newfoundland, then got refined in Britain.

answers.name: Golden retriever
answers.fact: Developed in the Scottish Highlands in the 1800s.

answers.name: German shepherd
answers.fact: Britain renamed them 'Alsatians' after World War I to avoid sounding German.

answers.name: Poodle
answers.fact: The name comes from the German 'pudel', to splash. It's France's national dog anyway.

answers.name: Bulldog
answers.fact: Originally bred for bull-baiting, which England banned in 1835.

answers.name: Chihuahua
answers.fact: Named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua.

answers.name: Pug
answers.fact: Kept as companions by Chinese emperors for many centuries.

answers.name: Beagle
answers.fact: The classic airport sniffer dog. Snoopy is one too.

answers.name: Siberian husky
answers.fact: Sled dogs relayed diphtheria serum to Nome, Alaska in 1925: the run that made Balto famous.

answers.name: Rottweiler
answers.fact: Named after Rottweil in Germany, where they drove cattle to market.

answers.name: Dachshund
answers.fact: 'Badger dog' in German: bred to dig badgers out of their burrows.

answers.name: Shiba Inu
answers.fact: The face of the 'doge' meme was a Shiba called Kabosu.

answers.name: Xoloitzcuintli
answers.fact: Mexico's ancient hairless dog, named after the Aztec god Xolotl.

answers.name: Corgi
answers.fact: Queen Elizabeth II owned around 30 Pembroke corgis over her reign.

answers.name: French bulldog
answers.fact: Overtook the Labrador as the most-registered breed in the US in 2022.

answers.name: Border collie
answers.fact: One named Chaser learned the names of over 1,000 toys.

answers.name: Boxer
answers.fact: Possibly named for the way it spars with its front paws.

answers.name: Great Dane
answers.fact: Actually German, not Danish. Scooby-Doo is one.

answers.name: Dalmatian
answers.fact: Puppies are born pure white; the spots come in over the first weeks.

answers.name: Dobermann
answers.fact: Bred in the 1890s by a German tax collector, Louis Dobermann, for protection.

answers.name: Cocker spaniel
answers.fact: Named for hunting woodcock.

answers.name: Springer spaniel
answers.fact: Bred to 'spring' game birds out of cover.

answers.name: Jack Russell terrier
answers.fact: Named after Reverend John Russell, a fox-hunting English parson.

answers.name: Yorkshire terrier
answers.fact: Bred to catch rats in Yorkshire's mills.

answers.name: Maltese
answers.fact: One of the oldest toy breeds, kept by ancient Greeks and Romans.

answers.name: Shih Tzu
answers.fact: 'Little lion' in Chinese.

answers.name: Pomeranian
answers.fact: Queen Victoria's love of small ones helped shrink the breed.

answers.name: Bichon frise
answers.fact: 'Frisé' means curly in French.

answers.name: Cavalier King Charles spaniel
answers.fact: Named after King Charles II, who was rarely without his spaniels.

answers.name: Boston terrier
answers.fact: One of the first breeds developed in the USA.

answers.name: Staffordshire bull terrier
answers.fact: The 'staffy' is regularly one of Australia's most popular breeds.

answers.name: American pit bull terrier
answers.fact: The UKC registered it in 1898. The AKC never has.

answers.name: Greyhound
answers.fact: The fastest dog breed, hitting around 70 km/h.

answers.name: Whippet
answers.fact: Nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse'.

answers.name: Saint Bernard
answers.fact: Alpine rescue dogs, but the little brandy barrel is a myth.

answers.name: Newfoundland
answers.fact: Webbed feet and a water-resistant coat make it a natural lifeguard.

answers.name: Labradoodle
answers.fact: First bred in Australia in 1989 as a guide dog. Its creator later said he regretted it.

answers.name: Cavoodle
answers.fact: Cavalier crossed with poodle, and an Australian favourite.

answers.name: Cockapoo
answers.fact: One of the original 'designer' crosses, popular in the US since the 1960s.

answers.name: Schnauzer
answers.fact: 'Schnauze' is German for snout. Hence the moustache.

answers.name: Bernese mountain dog
answers.fact: Swiss farm dogs that once pulled carts of milk and cheese.

answers.name: Australian shepherd
answers.fact: Despite the name, developed in the American West.

answers.name: Australian cattle dog
answers.fact: The oldest dog on record, Bluey (1910–1939), was one. So is the cartoon Bluey.

answers.name: Kelpie
answers.fact: Australian sheepdogs that will run across the sheep's backs to get ahead.

answers.name: Samoyed
answers.fact: Its upturned smile is said to stop drool from freezing into icicles.

answers.name: Akita
answers.fact: Hachikō, who waited at Shibuya Station for years after his owner died, was an Akita.

answers.name: Chow chow
answers.fact: It has a blue-black tongue.

answers.name: Shar pei
answers.fact: The loose wrinkly skin was meant to make it hard to grip in a fight.

answers.name: Bloodhound
answers.fact: Its tracking has been accepted as evidence in US courts.

answers.name: Basset hound
answers.fact: 'Bas' is French for low.

answers.name: Weimaraner
answers.fact: Nicknamed the 'grey ghost' for its silvery coat.

answers.name: Rhodesian ridgeback
answers.fact: Bred in southern Africa to hold lions at bay for hunters.

answers.name: Irish setter
answers.fact: Bred in Ireland to find game birds and 'set', or crouch, to show where they are.

answers.name: Afghan hound
answers.fact: Picasso had one called Kabul.

answers.name: Mastiff
answers.fact: A mastiff named Zorba weighed about 155 kg in 1989.

answers.name: Bull terrier
answers.fact: That egg-shaped head is unique. Target's mascot is one.

answers.name: West Highland terrier
answers.fact: Bred white, so hunters wouldn't mistake them for foxes.

answers.name: Scottish terrier
answers.fact: The dog token in Monopoly is a Scottie.

answers.name: Old English sheepdog
answers.fact: Nicknamed 'bobtail' for its traditionally short tail.

answers.name: Shetland sheepdog
answers.fact: Looks like a mini collie, but it's its own breed from the Shetland Islands.

answers.name: Rough collie
answers.fact: Lassie was a rough collie, always played by male dogs.

answers.name: Alaskan malamute
answers.fact: Alaska's official state dog.

answers.name: Pekingese
answers.fact: Legend says it's the child of a lion and a marmoset.

answers.name: Lhasa apso
answers.fact: Kept as indoor sentinels in Tibetan monasteries.

answers.name: Papillon
answers.fact: 'Butterfly' in French, for the shape of its ears.

answers.name: Cane corso
answers.fact: An Italian guardian breed that nearly died out in the 20th century.

answers.name: German shorthaired pointer
answers.fact: Pointers freeze and aim their nose straight at hidden game.

answers.name: Airedale terrier
answers.fact: The biggest terrier, nicknamed the 'King of Terriers'.

answers.name: Basenji
answers.fact: The 'barkless dog': it yodels instead.

answers.name: Saluki
answers.fact: One of the oldest breeds, with lookalikes in ancient Egyptian art.

answers.name: Borzoi
answers.fact: Bred by Russian aristocrats to hunt wolves.

answers.name: Irish wolfhound
answers.fact: The tallest dog breed on average.

answers.name: Puli
answers.fact: Its coat naturally twists into dreadlocks.

answers.name: Bedlington terrier
answers.fact: Looks like a lamb. Is not a lamb.

answers.name: Leonberger
answers.fact: Bred in Leonberg to look like the lion on the town's crest.

answers.name: Tibetan mastiff
answers.fact: One reportedly sold in China for about US$1.5 million in 2011.

answers.name: Kooikerhondje
answers.fact: Used to lure ducks into traps by waving its fluffy tail.

answers.name: Pharaoh hound
answers.fact: Malta's national dog. Its nose and ears flush pink when it's excited.

answers.name: Lagotto Romagnolo
answers.fact: Italy's truffle-hunting dog.

answers.name: Portuguese water dog
answers.fact: Bo and Sunny, the Obamas' White House dogs, were both Porties.

answers.name: Schipperke
answers.fact: 'Little skipper': it guarded barges on Belgian canals.

answers.name: Keeshond
answers.fact: Mascot of the Dutch Patriot party in the 1700s.

answers.name: Affenpinscher
answers.fact: 'Monkey terrier' in German. One named Banana Joe won Westminster in 2013.

answers.name: Brussels griffon
answers.fact: Often said to have inspired Chewbacca's look.

answers.name: Chinese crested
answers.fact: A regular winner of the 'World's Ugliest Dog' contest.

answers.name: Italian greyhound
answers.fact: Frederick the Great was buried beside his.

answers.name: Coton de Tulear
answers.fact: Called the royal dog of Madagascar.

answers.name: Dandie Dinmont terrier
answers.fact: The only breed named after a fictional character, from a Walter Scott novel.

answers.name: Border terrier
answers.fact: Bred on the England–Scotland border to bolt foxes.

answers.name: Cairn terrier
answers.fact: Toto in The Wizard of Oz was a Cairn named Terry.

answers.name: Belgian Malinois
answers.fact: A favourite of military units worldwide.

answers.name: Briard
answers.fact: Thomas Jefferson brought Briards to America.

answers.name: Great Pyrenees
answers.fact: Guards flocks in the mountains between France and Spain.

answers.name: Anatolian shepherd
answers.fact: Used in Namibia to keep cheetahs off livestock, which saves the cheetahs too.

answers.name: Kuvasz
answers.fact: A Hungarian guardian dog, white so shepherds could tell it from wolves.

answers.name: Jindo
answers.fact: One named Baekgu walked about 300 km back to its old home in 1993.

answers.name: Catahoula leopard dog
answers.fact: Louisiana's state dog.

answers.name: Plott hound
answers.fact: North Carolina's state dog.

answers.name: Australian terrier
answers.fact: One of the first breeds developed in Australia.

answers.name: Australian silky terrier
answers.fact: Bred from Yorkshire and Australian terriers.

answers.name: Tenterfield terrier
answers.fact: An Australian breed named after the NSW town of Tenterfield.

answers.name: Ibizan hound
answers.fact: A Balearic sighthound that can leap remarkably high from a standstill.

answers.name: Bouvier des Flandres
answers.fact: Ronald Reagan's dog Lucky was one.

answers.name: Norwegian Lundehund
answers.fact: Six toes per foot and fold-shut ears, bred for climbing cliffs after puffins.

answers.name: Mudi
answers.fact: A rare Hungarian herder, only recognised by the AKC in 2022.

answers.name: Peruvian Inca Orchid
answers.fact: A hairless sighthound that shows up on ancient Peruvian pottery.

answers.name: Kai Ken
answers.fact: Japan's brindled 'tiger dog' from the mountains of Yamanashi.

answers.name: Azawakh
answers.fact: A sighthound of the Sahel, kept by Tuareg nomads.

answers.name: Bergamasco shepherd
answers.fact: Its coat felts into flat mats called 'flocks'.

answers.name: Komondor
answers.fact: The Hungarian 'mop dog': its corded coat helped it blend in with the sheep it guarded.
